44281026.review:
I put about the same time into this as I did for HK - and in those 40 hours, Hollow Knight became one of my favourite, if not my number 1 choice for 2D action platformer. It became one of my favorite indies, in my top 3 for sure, and just in general gaming, definitely in my top 20 of all time. In those 40 hours I played HK I felt 90-95% of it was fun - sure there was some frustration here and there, but that’s par for the course right? A little bit of back tracking here and there, a few difficult bosses, even a couple of platforming challenges, and the true ending and path of pain all were incredible daunting, but I had fun throughout all of it and most my memories of that game are enjoyment and joy. I can’t say the same thing about silksong, and it’s a shame, because artistically this game is great. I firmly believe that challenging video games are awesome, (à la your sekiro’s, Celeste’s, bloodbornes, dark souls, cup heads etc) and often the victory you get from fighting those bosses, by identifying the attack patterns and gaps in their move set to exploit is almost unmatchable in how it scratches my brain. 

The exploration in those type of games are just as important, and if they don’t have any exploration, they should have something in them beyond the combat to keep players engaged and importantly they need to mitigate the back-tracking and “wasted time” (albeit all game’s inherently need some amount of back-tracking to create a sense of progression at times to show how strong the players are now compared to before, or for secrets and endings and the likes), and need to ensure the balanced “frustration” and “fun”. This is my opinion of course but, you are happy to take on the challenge because the game is fun to play. I think Team Cherry with their limited play-testing (you can find this in the credits and just by looking online), failed to identify the “fun” zone. It took me around 40 hours to get an ending and I can say maybe 60% of that was genuinely fun. The best part of the game in my opinion - the bosses - are kept away for annoying platforming, back-tracking and runs. I *want* to do your bosses Team Cherry that’s what brings me to these type of games, but if I feel like my 30 minutes that I’m stuck on a boss, if 5-8 minutes of those felt like I was just running back just to attempt it again, I can’t say that that was time well spent. I can’t for the life of me see myself wanting to touch this game any more than I have to - and after beating it, the thought of 100%ing for the first time feels like a chore, and I dread playing it for longer, and I’ve never really said that about any game. I want to love Silksong so much more than what I feel about it right now, and perhaps when the DLC comes I’ll give it another shot and continue my file to attempt 100% (or 112% or wtv) and maybe my mind will change then. 

With all of that said, I still 100% recommend this game - for both what it stands for as an indie game and what 3 developers have been able to achieve, and for what I believe it represents artistically and mechanically from a pure design perspective. Silk song for better or worse, is stubborn and sticks to its guns, and I can’t help but admire that. I know I’ll be back for my dose of pain from this game at some point, but until then, I’ll give this a begrudging “objective” rating of 8.5, but if I wanted to super honest and genuinely included how “fun” this game was for me and how much of it felt like I was making the most of my time, I’d probably knock it down by a point or two.

25194983.review:
BONJOUR MON AMI
After Beating (Verso Ending): This game coincidentally matched up after a period of intense grief and mental difficulty in my life, and then playing this beautiful game about grief and the acceptance of it, really clicked with me. I think this is the first game in a while that has achieved the 10/10. Music, graphics and characters were all amazing. The story was enthralling for the most part, and very well packaged within a 30-40 hour play-through. The side characters, and the world itself was gorgeous to explore, and had very linear level designs with some branching paths, which I thought was great for this style of game. I love my super massive open-worlds, but I think there is a place for games that go for this approach too. I think if a "indie" studio (they have several members with AAA experience), can produce this with a reasonable budget, and at a £40 price point, I genuinely wonder how I am ever going to justify £70-£80 pricing for the new Nintendo stuff.

The only point of concern: Do I think this game has "fixed" turn-based combat? No, that would imply there was something broken with that style of game-play, and ultimately its a preference thing between turn-based and real-time. I will say, it is a very fun mechanic and can push forward what we can expect from these kind of jrpg inspired games. But because it is so trivialized by lowering the difficulty, I wonder how many people actually needed to engage with it properly. 

I played on expedition difficulty, and found I had to parry or dodge 90% of the time in order to win fights, so I am glad it is a mechanic that is expected to be mastered on harder difficulties, but I did experiment with the parry-windows at different difficulties and noticed that the damage difference itself on missing a parry is so massive that on the easiest difficulty, you don't need to parry at all- which is fine obviously, but I think its a mechanic that has its place but isn't this grand-fix that people are claiming it to be, for turn-based games. I'm sure for people who can't stay concentrated on turn-based games as they would in a real-time game, it gives them something to stay engaged with, but for someone who loves both styles, I found the mechanic, neat but that's about it. I don't think games need to look at this system going-forward and think it is the definitive way to make turn-based games, because its not, it is however, a very novel way to engage players who can't normally sit through x amount of turns passively.
25194983.title: PlayStation 5

24802863.review:
Pt. Standard (2 Life Revive + Letter Grades).
What could have been a 9/10 is like maybe a 6.5 or 7/10. Awful because of the devs' bizarre pacing and choices of making an incredible action-combat style of game with really cool combos and inter-weaving of different styles of combat that it excels at, and forcing it to be a platformer? A puzzle-solver? What? 

It trips over itself every 10 minutes because the great combat and music it has gets ruined by random mini-games/puzzle solving side content that is forced to be main content so often. Chapter 8 or 9? Spend 10-15 minutes just cleaning up...???? Like the pacing of the game there was so intense, we're reaching the climax in a bit, but then it just gets derailed? I don't understand the choice of downtime in a game like this, especially in the last 1/4 of the game. So the good story and game-play you want to engage with has horrible pacing. Also 30fps for this style of game is awful but its whatever you can get used to it. On its own that would have been fine, but poor-performance at times, combined with the frustrating pacing and poor mini-games/puzzles in the main mission (like why are you including a stealth section, not just once but twice???). 

And the final boss? I don't understand because they had the choice to have made an amazing human vs human boss that forces you to dodge and combo chain etc., but instead is a platformer at the start???? Then turns into a mediocre beat this object up for lore reasons which is fine. Then the final phase which is the best phase which is good, but like, you had Jena's fight, which was incredible, fast-paced, dodge out of the way, work combos in, and kept you engaged but instead it was this sort-of-engaging projectile filled phase that is meh at best, and annoying at worst. It's so frustrating because this game has amazing music, fun characters, engaging voice-acting with an alright story, things that would have combined for an 8 or maybe 9/10 if you really enjoyed the plot (again I thought it was ok but the combat was so fun). And then decides to force mechanics like puzzle/platforming/stealth, in an action game whose biggest strength is the flow of combat, and that would be okay if they were at least fun or interesting. But they're bare-bones, they barely take anytime to do and are a chore that gets in the way of the actually engaging fights. I want to love this game, but because it tied its shoes together and keeps falling over every few steps, 7/10.

I like the story and characters and their growth over the 20-25 hour play through. The music is banging, Mr. Meguro you are a genius in all your games and this was no exception. Atmosphere and writing and general vibes, were great. HOWEVER, the gameplay. It's...... fine. Besides the random-encounter every 5 steps, its fun enough for what it is but generally pretty easy. Though, full warning, this is an oldschool JRPG, save as much as you can whenever you can, and don't be afraid to use guides if you need it. Because team-wipes can and will happen and you will hate yourself for not saving earlier. The final boss is a dumpster fire (only mechanically; story/graphically it's amazing). You should fully be prepared to grind out in the final level/get the ultimate personas via the good ending and choosing the right options because stupid thing has 15k health and phase changers similar to p3 fes final boss. 

So what are my issues with it? A really good story hidden behind a tedious game-play loop is just frustrating. It's a relic of its time, and for better or worse, it sticks with it and doesn't deviate at any point. I liked it somewhat. Also it has incredible world-building (for its time!) if you go out and talk to everyone/interact with every item that the !!! on it to show you can do that. The side characters have a lot of story that you won't see if you don't go out of your way to find them, but sometimes feels shallow/falls flat. 7/10 BUT, I can't recommend this to most people unless they A) Love persona/SMT B) Love J-RPGS and Dungeon Crawler Style Old school games with random encounters or alternatively none of the above and C) Are kinda a masochist like me. Jokes aside, this game is good but flawed and has made me way more open to this genre/time period of RPGs, but is for a niche audience compared to p3 p4 and p5, and that's fine. 

Side-note: whole trope of a big God leading the antagonist astray/being the big reveal is kinda getting tiring atlus, at least p5 royal had some uniqueness to its true ending (i.e., final boss), so I'm hoping more of that style of an actual antagonist themselves at some point.

13871444.review:
TL:DR It's solid, i give it 7.5/10. Played on hard. Not my first "Yakuza" game but is my first in the Kiriyu/Majima era, since I played like a dragon first (Ichiban is just so wholesome) 

(I may play through it again on Legendary to see if that makes me feel like the combat forces me to think a bit more, in which case I will update this if needed.)

Kinda mixed feelings. Story? 8.5/10. Characters? Generally speaking, Imperfect and flawed, but human, 8.5/10 (the leads at least, there are absolute scumbags like Oda who are terrible terrible people, fuck Oda all my homies hate Oda, but they are still written well, mostly).

Gameplay? Now here is where my main issue lies with this game. It's not bad, but, it feels repetitive even when I'm trying my hardest to try different essences/combat styles and switching between Majima and Kiriyu when possible to keep it fresh, but the enemy variety left a lot to be desired. The thing is, trying out the different combat styles was fun, but the enemies didn't feel like a challenge even on the hard besides maybe the first time you encounter (spoilers: Kuze, since he will throw a little bit of a curve ball at you by doing what you did to everyone else, be a massive hard rock whose main counter is the rush style to be able to quickly dodge). But even that fight took me maybe 5-10 mins before i figured out I could quickly dodge out of the way and treat it like a boxing match. And it was cool, but those "A-HA!" moments were rare, and as someone whose so used to challenging combat like Sekiro (I am aware these are not even remotely the same genre of games), it felt a bit frustrating. I have heard that Yakuza 3 (?) on hard mode is really difficult so I look forward to that, and I'll probably restrict my item usage to make it even more fun, but this game left a little to be desired in the combat department. It's serviceable, and I did have a lot of fun with the Breaker style and Beast style, but it felt a bit shallow. Not a victory I got by being good at the game, but more so just a satisfying thing to knock around goons here and there. CLIMAX BATTLES HOWEVER, are where the game really shines with scenarios that are a little bit more unique in a way by suggesting certain rules for you, which was super interesting but again, nothing I would say is 10/10, just a solid 7. 

Overall this game is a fantastic playthrough that has very dark moments, but showcases hope and re-thinks what it means to be a "masculine man", as cliche as that sounds. Kiriyu shows emotions, he cries, Majima cries, Makoto cries, they laugh, they lose friends, they go through so much pain (Majima and Makoto's backstories are just gut-wrenching) and that scene when the two siblings "re-unite", you know which one I'm talking about, genuinely made me have tears in my eyes. A good solid game overall. 7.5/10 without climax battles, 8/10 with.

So I dropped this around 2020, and came back to it in 2024, and well. It's good, better than when I first played it. The story and ambience etc. have always been good, the gameplay is serviceable (its from the PS3/Xbox360 Era so I get it, its not great now but its not bad). I think it was a massive step forward in terms of morality story telling at the time, but it sort of falls short when you've seen so much of it in the modern era.

Plot twist was fine, kinda predictable. I think its good, 8/10, but you have to be in the mindset of, "this is the first of its kind", and accept its flaws to appreciate it. Otherwise it sort of becomes repetitive, even though its not, because it was the setting stone for the atmosphere and horror-esque elements we like today. Go into it without spoilers as otherwise you lose any element of suspense, because it is quite story driven for an FPS. I can appreciate what it has done for the industry but not something I would consider a greatest game of all time, because good gameplay will always be king.
